notes.title: Neverseas - Developer's Log №6
notes.content:
[h1]Galleon — the Glory of the Neverseas[/h1][hr][/hr][p][b]Galleon[/b] — a large multi-deck sailing ship of the 16th–18th centuries with substantial artillery armament, used both as a warship and a merchant vessel. The origin of the word [i]“galleon”[/i] goes back to the Spanish [i]“galeón”[/i], which is an augmentative form of the Latin [i]“galea”[/i] — “galley.” In other words, a galleon is essentially a “large galley.”[/p][p]The galleon was the most advanced type of sailing vessel that appeared in the 16th century. This type of sailing ship emerged through the evolution of the [i]caravel[/i] and was intended for long ocean voyages. Combining a full-rigged setup (three masts) and a large hold, the galleon became one of the most sought-after ships of its time.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/e217fb2c8a0f5159b18272e8d7bac0d4ce5c0ede.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The reduction of the forecastle superstructure and the elongation of the hull led to an increase in [i]stability[/i] (a measure of a ship’s steadiness on the water — in fact, it was due to problems with stability that the Swedish [i]Vasa[/i] sank on her maiden voyage upon leaving port), as well as to a reduction in wave resistance. As a result, the galleon turned into a faster and more maneuverable seagoing vessel. The galleon differed from earlier ships in that it was longer, lower, and straighter, with a square stern instead of a rounded one.[/p][hr][/hr][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/521a46879da834cf8edb284b9702b1ee38444894.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][p]Once upon a time, we could not even think that we would get together and create such a concept for you. We read books about sea voyages to the holes, watched the same movies hundreds of times, and still didn't even know each other. But, as the morning salty breeze refreshes, so we were introduced and united by the craving for the sea, its dark depths and the treasures of uninhabited islands, the trials of which are amenable only to the brave.[/p][p]Our creator, Alexey "AVG" Vasiliev, created another work of art for us.:[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][carousel][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/bdab5f09954973794455be20e7e0e02ac111ab64.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/5fccbba0e1d39667611385091db9fb9ded204f75.png"][/img][/carousel][p]He is the ruler of the seas and oceans. He is impeccable both in the port, which has assembled the rigging, and at the zero meridian in complete calm. An aggressive conqueror of the waves flaps the sails in anticipation of a tailwind:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/b63494d8a8f3cb8dd0332c8cb17e5195c322614e.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][i]- The galleon becomes the basis of the fleets of the Spaniards and the British. The stem, strongly curved and elongated forward, had decorations and resembled those of galleys in shape. The long bowsprit carried a blind sail. The forward superstructure was pushed back and did not hang over the stem, as in the karakka.[/i][/p][hr][/hr][carousel][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/c9dd851fe6fc205957827f68485c7e7adf0fbaed.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/e08aef30fc30e3ca4604739ed9606ea4fd1498bf.png"][/img][/carousel][p][i]- The aft superstructure, tall and narrow, was located on the cut-off stern. The superstructure had several tiers, which housed the living quarters of officers and passengers.  The heavily sloped stern had a transom above the cargo waterline. The stern was decorated with carvings and balconies.[/i][/p][hr][/hr][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/04c970181dda37637b6e6a477a4b39ac8e488319.png"][/img][i]- Depending on the displacement, galleons were built with a number of decks from two to seven. The side of the vessel from the keel to the cargo waterline had a large collapse, and to the upper deck there was a blockage. At the same time, several tasks were solved: the load capacity increased, the transition from ship to ship during boarding became more difficult, the overall strength increased; the force of the waves hitting the side was softened, since the wave was reflected upward, and the hull did not experience its direct impact.[/i][/p][hr][/hr][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/5dc27c440963f58594624cbcfd81a4f5668d1f4a.png"][/img][i]- The galleon was armed with up to 30 guns of caliber from 3-pounders (6 cm) to 50-pounders (19 cm) and a significant number (up to 100) portable blunderbusses for firing through loopholes from the gallery of the aft superstructure and the upper floors of the bow superstructure. It was on the galleon that the guns were first installed both above and below the main deck, which led to the appearance of battery (cannon) decks, the guns stood on the sides and fired through the ports. As a result, cargo transportation facilities were significantly reduced. The displacement of the largest Spanish galleons reached 1,000 tons or more, length 50 meters (37 meters at the keel), width 12 meters. There were 50-80 guns on two battery decks. Over time, the size and armament of the galleons grew.[/i][/p][hr][/hr][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/385e512364fbb44ffc78a51528deca6d5e5269c3.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][p]Once again:[/p][carousel][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/cb47ca9f3e5ef17c7a3dbbd7a84176555ab95ba8.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/9edf6463b853cd93543799f7889f7c34cfcce0ce.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/c43a21c03ecfb43056051f23695fea653d7779de.png"][/img][/carousel][p]The stern, and a lot of carved elements:[/p][carousel][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/a509aed14b1a47920da6fc52fb25a6bc06e4bd92.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/ec923f3839ec45470f8b4eeb9065685b27be226f.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/84f37b4f61dbf059fc2734b06cbd5dea792ec4e6.png"][/img][/carousel][p]And even the sides of the conqueror of the elements had time to get tired of taking the blows of the waves and were overgrown with shells.:[/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/6563b58bce0ee98543451b40e4d50d33e8359dfe.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][p]Well, we are sure that we have done a great job. We hope you will appreciate it.[/p][p]Let the wind blow through the salt-soaked hair of the captains, and the gaze rushes over the horizon. And the Galleon will become a reliable assistant in this difficult path, because with its power it is quite capable of changing the balance of power in a difficult confrontation. Ahoy![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/675aeb35f439c0b5cd4b960cd18e28c05bf19dc6.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Fair winds and bright victories in naval battles![/b][/p][p]If you like our project idea and what we’re working on, please support us in the way that’s convenient for you:[/p][p]💬 [url="https://boosty.to/neverseas"]Boosty[/url] [/p][p]🎁 [url="https://www.patreon.com/c/Neverseas"]Patreon[/url][/p][hr][/hr][p][b][i]Thank you for reading to the end![/i][/b][/p][p][b][i]Sincerely, the Neverseas development team[/i][/b][/p][p]
[/p]

The long bowsprit carried a blind sail. The forward superstructure was pushed back and did not hang over the stem, as in the karakka.

The aft superstructure, tall and narrow, was located on the cut-off stern. The superstructure had several tiers, which housed the living quarters of officers and passengers.  The heavily sloped stern had a transom above the cargo waterline. The stern was decorated with carvings and balconies.

Depending on the displacement, galleons were built with a number of decks from two to seven. The side of the vessel from the keel to the cargo waterline had a large collapse, and to the upper deck there was a blockage. At the same time, several tasks were solved: the load capacity increased, the transition from ship to ship during boarding became more difficult, the overall strength increased; the force of the waves hitting the side was softened, since the wave was reflected upward, and the hull did not experience its direct impact.

The galleon was armed with up to 30 guns of caliber from 3-pounders (6 cm) to 50-pounders (19 cm) and a significant number (up to 100) portable blunderbusses for firing through loopholes from the gallery of the aft superstructure and the upper floors of the bow superstructure. It was on the galleon that the guns were first installed both above and below the main deck, which led to the appearance of battery (cannon) decks, the guns stood on the sides and fired through the ports. As a result, cargo transportation facilities were significantly reduced. The displacement of the largest Spanish galleons reached 1,000 tons or more, length 50 meters (37 meters at the keel), width 12 meters. There were 50-80 guns on two battery decks. Over time, the size and armament of the galleons grew.
And the Galleon will become a reliable assistant in this difficult path, because with its power it is quite capable of changing the balance of power in a difficult confrontation.

notes.title: Neverseas - Developer's Log №5
notes.content:
[h1]Ahoy, Captains[b]![/b][/h1][hr][/hr][p]The sailing ship of the XVI–XVIII century is an incredibly complex technological object. The construction of the new sailing ship was an event, the result of the hard work of a huge number of people.[/p][p]The sailing ship was built taking into account the fact that it would spend most of its shipboard "life" on a raid – in battles, or off foggy distant shores, or, loaded to the waterline, scurrying back and forth - in a word, beneficial. Repairs and upgrades - "simple" in the port - were expensive for shipping companies.[/p][p]To increase the degree of autonomy, some of the maintenance tasks were transferred from the port to the ship, for example, workshops were set up.[/p][p]Workshops on sailing ships performed several important functions. They were used to repair sails, rigging and other important elements of the ship, as the sails could tear or wear out, and they needed to be repaired in a timely manner. The workshops also produced new sails, ropes and other parts necessary to maintain the ship's combat capability. This made it possible to prepare spare parts and materials, which was especially important during long sea voyages. On shore or in port, workshops provided the opportunity to carry out the necessary work to modernize and improve the design and equipment of the vessel. In addition, they served as a place to train crew members in the necessary skills related to ship repair and maintenance. Thus, the presence of workshops on sailing ships significantly increased their efficiency and readiness to perform tasks.[/p][hr][/hr][p]Let's turn to one of the best representatives in history – HMS Victory, a 104-gun battleship of the first rank of the Royal Navy of Great Britain.:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/93f800cf7f6d2c022ecf2f69fc44919e6609578a.png"][/img][/p][p]HMS Victory had various workshops, each of which performed specialized functions.:[/p][p]1. Sail Workshop[/p][p]Sails were made and repaired in this workshop. Ship carpenters here worked with various fabrics to create reliable and durable sails for efficient sailing.[/p][p]2. Tackle Workshop[/p][p]This workshop was engaged in the production and repair of ropes, chains and other elements of gear. It was critically important for sailing a sailing vessel, as the correct adjustment of the rigging ensured the maneuverability and safety of the ship.[/p][p]3. Carpenter's workshop[/p][p]The carpentry workshop carried out work on the repair and maintenance of the wooden structure of the ship. Carpenters repaired damage to the hull, as well as carried out work to improve the interior.[/p][p]4. Gunsmiths Workshop[/p][p]The ship's artillery armament was maintained and repaired here. The gunsmiths monitored the condition of the cannons and other weapons, which was important for their combat capability.[/p][p]5. Workshop of glaziers and coppersmiths[/p][p]These workshops were engaged in the maintenance of glass and copper elements on the ship. The workers updated and repaired the windows, and also dealt with the copper parts that were used in various mechanisms.[/p][p]Each of these workshops played an important role in maintaining the functionality of HMS Victory and ensuring its readiness for combat operations.[/p][hr][/hr][p]It is clear from the history itself that the installation and development of workshops on the ship is not just a secondary option or a cosmetic improvement. This is the basis of true autonomy, survivability and strategic flexibility of a player in a naval game. A ship without workshops is like an army without a rear: it is strong, but until the first serious battle, after which it becomes vulnerable, dependent on ports, resources and finances.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/34787ea1612f1e14396485ed3c43f7152e441ffe.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Workshop system on board[/b][/p][p]After studying real-world examples, we were transported to the world of Neverseas and delved into the development of various deck improvements that affect the ship's combat capability, survivability, and economy.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]1. Carpentry workshop[/b][/p][p]Carpentry workshop allows the player not to be afraid of holes and storms, because the ship will be able to repair the damage itself. This is especially important when the game offers long-range raids in hostile waters, where the nearest friendly port may be at a considerable distance. Instead of retreating, wasting time and money on repairs, the player continues his voyage, maintains his pace and gains an advantage over less prepared enemies.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/f8905f4083aebe0fe1454835521f3ea44420195c.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Appointment:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Hull repairs during combat or on the move (out of port)[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Accelerated recovery after rams and storms[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Reduced chance of sinking from critical damage[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p][b]2. Sailing and rope workshop[/b][/p][p]The sailing workshop provides more than just speed. It makes maneuvers sharper, accelerates turns, helps to catch up and escape. If the sails are damaged in battle, the sailboat's crew will be able to repair them without losing steam. This means that the ship will not be helpless in the middle of a battle or on the high seas, which is especially important in a chase or during a storm. And in an environment where every choice affects the outcome of a battle, even a small increase in speed or maneuverability can decide the fate of a battle.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/b7fd4f986f2cb93d2b484bcff43689f30ae2aea2.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Appointment:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Repair and manufacture of sails on the go[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Ship speed boost[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Improved maneuverability, reduced turnaround time[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p][b]3. Forge[/b][/p][p]The forge, which looks less obvious, actually turns out to be critical. In battle, guns wear out, get knocked down, their fastenings weaken, and without a forge you can be left with inoperable weapons. The forge can even forge special ammunition — chain ammunition, buckshot, red-hot cores — giving the player additional tactical options. Not to mention the repair of anchors, metal hull rims, and even grappling hooks.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/d6b32072e9c340202526e7d526b17d14dcfdc714.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Appointment:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Forging cannonballs, chain balls, red-hot shells[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Accelerated repair of guns and rigging[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Crafting unique ammunition[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p][b]4. Gunsmith's workshop[/b][/p][p]An armory is also very important, especially for those who rely on boarding. Without it, the crew quickly loses their combat capability: muskets rust, sabers blunt, flintlocks misfire. But with a gunsmith on board, boarding turns into a short, effective operation, unlike a bloodbath where the one with the most bodies wins.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/8c458672e2cb4da0c156242d01a0968326cdd47c.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Appointment:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Upgrade the team's weapons: muskets, pistols and sabers[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Increasing the effectiveness of boarding[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Speeding up the reloading of personal weapons[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p][b]5. Construction workshop[/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/597935d89353c3e4f78c8d57d299a242d1a7ef76.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Appointment:[/b][/p][list][*][p]The possibility of ship upgrades right at sea[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Reducing the cost of repairs at the port[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p]Thus, the addition of workshops and the development of appropriate mechanics opens up additional possibilities for fine-tuning the ship. Their presence provides not just “ship pumping”, but the opportunity to play out role-playing scenarios, collect builds for a certain style of play - a raider, a naval commander, a merchant or a corsair. You can not depend on ports and conduct long-term raids, because you are your own arsenal, shipyard and repair dock.[/p][p]It is the workshops that turn the ship not into a disposable cannon, but into a real combat platform capable of operating independently at sea for a long time, modifying on the move and adapting to changing conditions.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h2]We also answered your questions:[/h2][h3][b]Q: [/b]What are the key features of the in-game economy when interacting with players and NPC factions?[/h3][p][b]A:[/b] In the current concept, all players in a session are automatically aligned with the faction of the session leader. For example, if you've pledged allegiance to Spain in your game and then join a friend who has chosen France — your loyalty will reflect their choice. This can lead to unexpected diplomatic situations, including hostility from certain NPC factions.[/p][p]As for the economy itself, it operates on a unified principle: every action in the game has a cost — whether it’s trading, hiring, repairing, or purchasing. [/p][p]Example:[/p][list][*][p]A faction focused on naval expansion may offer cheaper ships and crew, but charge significantly more for rare resources or unique goods. [/p][/*][*][p]A trade-oriented faction might give discounts on raw materials but demand higher prices for protection and weaponry. Prices may vary depending on the characteristics of each faction, but overall, the economic system is designed to be balanced.[/p][/*][/list][p]The main difference between NPC factions and players lies in their starting positions: NPC factions are already integrated into the global economy with established assets and networks, while the player starts from scratch with a single ship and must gradually work their way into that system through gameplay.[/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Q: [/b]How much will player reputation and choices influence relationships with factions and overall story progression?[/h3][p][b]A:[/b] Reputation plays a key role — including determining narrative branches and triggering global changes in the game world. By performing certain actions — whether positive or provocative — players will gain or lose reputation points with specific factions.[/p][p]This directly affects:[/p][list][*][p]the range of available goods;[/p][/*][*][p]services;[/p][/*][*][p]access to unique faction quests;[/p][/*][*][p]and how NPCs react to the player on the map.[/p][/*][/list][p]For example, if a player is known as an enemy of a faction, their ships might attack on sight without hesitation. In this way, player decisions don't just impact the storyline — they shape how the world reacts to them on a fundamental level.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Q: [/b]What will ship control feel like — more of an arcade or a simulation[b]?[/b][/h3][p]
[b]A:[/b] This is one of the most nuanced and debated aspects of the game. We're aiming for a balance within the "easy to learn, hard to master" philosophy. On the one hand, ship control should allow players to showcase skill and feel like real captains. On the other, we don’t want players to feel like they need to take real-world sailing courses just to play the game.[/p][p]That’s why we’re designing a system that’s accessible to newcomers but still offers depth for those who want to master it. Players who want to get the most out of their ship will truly be able to do so — through precise handling, tactical awareness, and attention to detail. And of course, we'll be carefully monitoring feedback and balance as development continues.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Fair winds and bright victories in naval battles![/b][/p][p]If you like our project idea and what we’re working on, please support us in the way that’s convenient for you:[/p][p]💬 [url="https://boosty.to/neverseas"]Boosty[/url] [/p][p]🎁 [url="https://www.patreon.com/c/Neverseas"]Patreon[/url][/p][hr][/hr][p][b][i]Thank you for reading to the end![/i][/b][/p][p][b][i]Sincerely, the Neverseas development team[/i][/b][/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Neverseas - Developer's Log №4
notes.content:
[h1]Ahoy, Captains[b]![/b][/h1][hr][/hr][p]Today we’re diving into the ship armament system of Neverseas. This topic turned out to be so broad and complex that it sparked numerous heated discussions and several complete overhauls and redesigns.[/p][p]The main challenge was that the 16th–18th centuries marked a true revolution in the development of firearms and naval artillery. A vast array of weaponry emerged—from massive bombards and small-caliber mortars to falconets and demi-cannons. These technological advancements drastically altered naval warfare, opening new tactical and strategic possibilities. This revolutionary period was followed by relentless testing and field trials, where sometimes an admiral’s strategic brilliance was paid for by the lives of many brave sailors.[/p][p]Our goal was to maintain historical authenticity and variety while crafting engaging game mechanics that would make each weapon feel distinct and genuinely authentic.[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/3dae5c33f1fdff7350972085d55cfd3bd81ca0f3.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][p]To implement such a wide variety of ballistic systems, we developed robust mathematical models and an intuitive user interface. Ship armaments were tied to specific slots, each corresponding to a particular deck and position on board.[/p][p]While this approach allowed for extensive customization, it unfortunately turned out to be overly cumbersome, especially on ships equipped with numerous cannons. Setting up, managing, and keeping track of each cannon’s unique characteristics quickly became tiresome and uncomfortable for players.[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/0d10c32a8e6289f42a7187e9e5fbe7c62856b175.jpg"][/img]In the image, you can see the initial interface prototypes for interacting with the weapon mounting system.[/p][hr][/hr][p]We were forced to retrace our steps and choose an entirely different path. We completely reworked the system: smaller weapons were handed over to the crew's control, requiring players to set priority targets. The main weapons were unified by ship sides and standardized. This decision greatly simplified installation and management, but unfortunately, gameplay lost depth due to lengthy reload times of the main weapons and limited flexibility for detailed combat adjustments. This forced us to rethink our approach once again.[/p][p]We wanted to resolve this issue decisively, leaving no room for doubt. We studied how armament was arranged on real ships of that era:[/p][list][*][p]On the main gundeck (lower gun deck), heavy demi-cannons and culverins were positioned to maintain a low center of gravity.[/p][/*][*][p]Medium-caliber weapons—falconets and lighter demi-cannons—were mounted on the forecastle and quarterdeck.[/p][/*][*][p]Small-caliber weapons were located on the upper decks (foredeck and stern), intended to target enemy crews and damage their rigging.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/98872ae8ebbf02390aec52bf3da51338ffa44180.png"][/img][/p][p]Our battleship in cross-section is still a work in progress, but as a demonstrator of the differences between weapons on different decks, it’s absolutely ideal.[/p][hr][/hr][p]The main distinction from previous, less convenient systems is that we’ve taken control of light armament away from the crew and implemented a convenient “360° view” when aiming. The primary guns have been divided into different groups by caliber. When a target moves from one sector to another, the game automatically switches you to the weapons on the appropriate broadside and selects the best type of armament.[/p][p]We now consider this implementation optimal and hope it stays that way for a long time. =)[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][table equalcells="1" colwidth=","][tr][th][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/798a3cd2d916dc157e6f4b819048d619e9a691e8.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][/th][th][p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/6552ee0d7e51003e9071580eff3fc2672e42f68b.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][/th][/tr][/table][p]An illustration with cats perfectly demonstrates the variety of installed weapons.[/p][hr][/hr][p]Firing from small-caliber guns has eliminated the tedious wait for the main cannons to reload. Thanks to the precision and excellent ballistics of these weapons, you can effectively hit specific modules of enemy ships. We also added two new mechanics:[/p][list][*][p]The ability to fire either in volleys or single shots.[/p][/*][*][p]The option to choose the firing sequence: bow-to-stern, stern-to-bow, or maximum rate of fire with minimal pauses between shots.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p]Additionally, we’ve introduced mortars, significantly expanding tactical possibilities.[/p][p]Now players have four weapon types at their disposal:[/p][p][/p][h2]Main Guns[/h2][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/dcfcc0b721571e156190a2b0c97a92cc20fa78e1.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Heavy artillery that not all ships carry, and acquiring such weaponry is always challenging since it’s reserved mainly for military use.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h2]Medium Guns[/h2][carousel][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/f9e575f0c2284d90b5f1065341f880c24a87a64f.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/63c97d56393d6a7ec29775c31194c8eac32bc520.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][img src="data:image/png;base64,"][/img][/p][p]These or similar types are installed on almost all ships that have space for them.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h2]Small‑Caliber Guns[/h2][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/349a5fcb467975a44d71e31b909acfb0781713f8.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The most widespread weapons, found on any ship. Deck armament is widely used on vessels ranging from small boats to battleships.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h2]Mortars[/h2][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45021039/b84b3e68342df3ed43c34d4036a82173aecd5299.jpg"][/img] [/p][p]Weapons firing on a high trajectory, ideal for siege operations.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h3]In the end, we achieved a dynamic and varied gameplay experience[/h3][list][*][p]Players must plan their approach tactics for effective broadside salvos;[/p][/*][*][p]Precisely target enemy ship modules using small‑caliber armament;[/p][/*][*][p]Fire ahead at long range using mortars.[/p][/*][/list][p]Although the main guns still have a realistic long reload time (30–40 seconds), the variety of weapons and well-balanced mechanics make the gameplay dynamic and virtually eliminate any sense of waiting.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h2]We also answered your questions:[/h2][h3][b]Q: Will there be different game modes?[/b][/h3][p][b]A:[/b] A good question. As with many elements in our game, we had many ideas:[/p][list][*][p]Different modes selectable when creating a lobby;[/p][/*][*][p]No choice—just press play;[/p][/*][*][p]Dynamically assigned mode depending on the quest.[/p][/*][/list][p]Ultimately, since we maintain a networked lobby-based multiplayer model, we decided not to restrict players artificially. Therefore, when creating a lobby, you’ll be able to choose basic modes:[/p][list][*][p][b]Team Battle[/b] on preconfigured maps and ships, where the mode may vary by map, but there will be no meta‑progression to pre‑prevent unfair play.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Standard Coop Mode[/b], where players will have access to all available progression and content we can create.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Q: Will there be anti-cheat in the game?[/b][/h3][p][b]A:[/b] Since we mentioned unfair players, the next question was this one. For a game primarily focused on coop with friends, we consider it unnecessary. If players discover a not-too-obvious exploit and enjoy using it, it can be considered an undocumented mechanic. :) Of course, we will fix obvious code bugs and balance issues so the gameplay doesn’t become too easy and the game keeps its edge.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Q: How much content is planned for launch?[/b][/h3][p]
[b]A:[/b] This question stumped us. Appetite, as they say, comes with eating. We have a set plan until early access launch and a tentative list of “wants” to implement afterward. It’s always tempting to add something new and interesting, but we mustn’t forget the content to support those mechanics. So, to summarize, for early access we plan to include:[/p][list][*][p]An autonomous economy (functionally ready, but needs visual polish and player interaction points);[/p][/*][*][p]2–3 game regions, each adding specific challenges for players. Since regions are separated by foggy seas affecting communication, entering each new region will feel like a New Game+;[/p][/*][*][p]An boarding system and fort siege mechanics;[/p][/*][*][p]Full land gameplay tightly integrated with naval gameplay, though priority remains sea combat;[/p][/*][*][p]A ship customization system;[/p][/*][*][p]Around 10 unique “social” islands, 15 quest-related islands, and 20 “lost” islands, providing small activities and PoIs;[/p][/*][*][p]Naval battles of course;[/p][/*][*][p]AI crew management, since they’ll handle the routine, not the player.[/p][/*][/list][p]This list isn’t exhaustive and will likely grow, but it’s our minimum program.[/p][p]TL;DR:[/p][p]Basic mechanics that let you feel like an adventurer and a ship captain![/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Fair winds and bright victories in naval battles![/b][/p][p]If you like our project idea and what we’re working on, please support us in the way that’s convenient for you:[/p][p]💬 [url="https://boosty.to/neverseas"]Boosty[/url] [/p][p]🎁 [url="https://www.patreon.com/c/Neverseas"]Patreon[/url][/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][b][i]Thank you for reading to the end![/i][/b][/p][p][b][i]Sincerely, the Neverseas development team[/i][/b][/p][p]
[/p]

tags.feature: The primary guns have been divided into different groups by caliber. When a target moves from one sector to another, the game automatically switches you to the weapons on the appropriate broadside and selects the best type of armament.
We now consider this implementation optimal and hope it stays that way for a long time. =)

Firing from small-caliber guns has eliminated the tedious wait for the main cannons to reload. Thanks to the precision and excellent ballistics of these weapons, you can effectively hit specific modules of enemy ships. We also added two new mechanics:
The ability to fire either in volleys or single shots.
The option to choose the firing sequence: bow-to-stern, stern-to-bow, or maximum rate of fire with minimal pauses between shots.
Additionally, we’ve introduced mortars, significantly expanding tactical possibilities.
Now players have four weapon types at their disposal:
Heavy artillery that not all ships carry, and acquiring such weaponry is always challenging since it’s reserved mainly for military use.
The most widespread weapons, found on any ship. Deck armament is widely used on vessels ranging from small boats to battleships.
Weapons firing on a high trajectory, ideal for siege operations.
Players must plan their approach tactics for effective broadside salvos;
Precisely target enemy ship modules using small‑caliber armament;
Fire ahead at long range using mortars.

Although the main guns still have a realistic long reload time (30–40 seconds), the variety of weapons and well-balanced mechanics make the gameplay dynamic and virtually eliminate any sense of waiting.
Different modes selectable when creating a lobby;
No choice—just press play;
Dynamically assigned mode depending on the quest.
Therefore, when creating a lobby, you’ll be able to choose basic modes:
Team Battle on preconfigured maps and ships, where the mode may vary by map, but there will be no meta‑progression to pre‑prevent unfair play.
Standard Coop Mode, where players will have access to all available progression and content we can create.

tags.bug: Of course, we will fix obvious code bugs and balance issues so the gameplay doesn’t become too easy and the game keeps its edge.

tags.feature: An autonomous economy (functionally ready, but needs visual polish and player interaction points);
2–3 game regions, each adding specific challenges for players. Since regions are separated by foggy seas affecting communication, entering each new region will feel like a New Game+;
An boarding system and fort siege mechanics;
Full land gameplay tightly integrated with naval gameplay, though priority remains sea combat;
A ship customization system;
Around 10 unique “social” islands, 15 quest-related islands, and 20 “lost” islands, providing small activities and PoIs;
Naval battles of course;
AI crew management, since they’ll handle the routine, not the player.
This list isn’t exhaustive and will likely grow, but it’s our minimum program.
Basic mechanics that let you feel like an adventurer and a ship captain!

notes.title: Neverseas - Developer's Log №3
notes.content:
[h1][b]Greetings, travelers![/b][/h1][hr][/hr][h2]Six bells on the watch — a new devlog rises on the horizon![/h2][p]
Two weeks have passed, and we’re back with fresh updates on the development of [i]Neverseas[/i]. Today, we continue the topic from our previous journal and dive deeper into the economic and political systems of the game world.[/p][p]Every team building an open-world game aims to make that world feel alive and dynamic — and we are no exception. Right now, we’re focused on creating an organic, responsive system that makes the seas of [i]Neverseas[/i] truly breathe.[/p][p]During your voyages, you’ll encounter a wide variety of ships — from lone merchants to armed escorts, from small caravans to entire fleets. Our goal is to ensure none of these encounters feel random. Every ship, convoy, or fleet you meet has a purpose: trading vessels follow orders from their home colonies, while warships act under the directives of their factions. It’s all part of a living system that reacts to the player’s actions and evolves with the world.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/b781f1b9abdf28bfcfdc935f100a69000caf5fd6.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]So, how does the economy of Neverseas work?[/b][/h3][p]Let’s start with the basics. The world map contains a fixed number of islands, each hosting one or more settlements. We call these settlements [i]colonies[/i] — it’s the most accurate term for their role in the system.[/p][p]At the beginning of the game, there’s little disparity in wealth or military strength between colonies. Each colony independently decides what buildings to construct and what path of development to follow. This level of management is what we call the [b]colonial level[/b].[/p][p]Multiple colonies can unite under a [b]faction[/b]. The faction oversees long-term strategies and makes high-level decisions for its member colonies — this is the [b]factional level[/b] of governance.[/p][p]A faction remains in existence as long as it controls at least one colony. Losing all colonies means the dissolution of the faction as a political force.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/1e260e1d725cb01cc347526ad381464c7ef498d5.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Now that we’ve covered the basics, let’s look at the system in action.[/b][/h3][p]At the [b]colonial level[/b], the driving force behind each colony is the desire to grow — to increase in size, wealth, and stability. Colonies are apolitical by nature: they are not interested in conflict or territorial expansion, only in prosperity and self-sufficiency.[/p][p]At the [b]factional level[/b], the goal shifts: factions strive to increase the number of colonies under their control. They operate strategically and aggressively — utilizing blockades, conquests, raids on trade routes, and full-scale military campaigns.[/p][p]It’s important to understand that while colonies and factions are connected, their goals don’t always align. This creates fertile ground for tension and dynamic conflict. Factions may push colonies toward war, while the colonies themselves prefer to build, trade, and thrive in peace.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Let’s look closer at the colonial level.[/b][/h3][p]As a colony’s population grows, it expands its industrial base and fortifications. This development depends on several factors:[/p][list][*][p]Its geographic proximity to other settlements[/p][/*][*][p]The terrain and climate of its island[/p][/*][*][p]The evolving needs of its population[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Industry[/b][/p][p]Industrial buildings serve two main purposes:[/p][olist][*][p][b]Meeting internal demands[/b] — As the population grows, so does the demand for goods, both in quantity and quality.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Generating profit through exports[/b] — Colonies sell surpluses to gain profit and purchase goods they lack, since no single island can provide for all its needs alone.[/p][/*][/olist][p][b]Defense[/b][/p][p]Defensive structures are built systematically, but their pace depends heavily on the political and military situation.
Colonies in peaceful factions or remote regions often deprioritize fortifications. In contrast, those near conflict zones or hostile territories tend to bolster their defenses much faster.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/bc78e91b5aadeb51af7f9ca184dffa20203fee21.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Now to the factional level.[/b][/h3][p]A [b]faction-state[/b] governs several colonies and makes key strategic decisions, including:[/p][list][*][p]Imposing trade restrictions (e.g. embargoes)[/p][/*][*][p]Organizing and coordinating naval fleets[/p][/*][*][p]Commissioning shipbuilding projects in member colonies[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Faction goals[/b][/p][p]The primary goal of a faction is to [b]protect its colonies[/b] and [b]expand its domain[/b] by conquering those of rival factions. While colonies focus inward, factions act outward — politically and militarily.[/p][p][b]Instruments of power[/b][/p][p]Factions can:[/p][list][*][p]Declare war on another faction[/p][/*][*][p]Propose peace or military alliances[/p][/*][*][p]Apply economic pressure by:[/p][list][*][p]Enforcing trade embargoes[/p][/*][*][p]Creating trade alliances that lower tariffs between partners, boosting mutual commerce[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]Factions play a central role in shaping the global economic and political climate of [i]Neverseas[/i], influencing both macroeconomic trends and the tides of naval warfare.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]What does this mean for the player?[/b][/h3][p]The system described above gives the player a wide range of tools to interact with the economic and political fabric of the [i]Neverseas[/i] world. You’re free to pursue your ambitions through trade and logistics, economic alliances, or military dominance — commanding fleets, besieging colonies, and eventually leading your own faction.[/p][p]The world of [i]Neverseas[/i] responds to your actions — and it’s up to you to decide whether to become a wise ruler, a shadowy trade baron, or a ruthless admiral feared across the seas.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]But what is trade without a proper workhorse?[/b][/h3][p]Meet the latest addition to the [i]Neverseas[/i] fleet — the sloop [b]“The Sea’s Shadow”[/b], crafted by our shipwright and 3D artist [b]Alexey “AVG” Vasiliev[/b]![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/fdc5775138a5836fc755659f12183837aacd6f6c.jpg"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][p]This single-masted vessel with a shallow draft is perfect for coastal trade between islands. It’s built to calmly haul cargo from bay to bay — yet still packs enough firepower to ward off shoreline thugs and hostile pursuers.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/a78dd384c51e07e0f6dcd75dc6684e29b0ea486f.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][p]Despite its modest size, the sloop features a surprisingly spacious hold and requires only a small crew — making it a highly flexible vessel. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/f337e3ac0a7fb3bbae27b1aac51fd35f271116b8.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][p]From beginner merchants to fleet support roles, its low construction and upkeep costs make it an accessible choice for traders of any scale.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/d98652957d2b017fb2ab2ca6c409ecc5d6c4e025.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][p]In designing this ship, we drew inspiration from a variety of small historical vessels — from dinghies and yawls to tenders and trade sloops. While there’s no single prototype, they all influenced the final design of the “[b]The Sea’s Shadow[/b]”.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/8e4f84740519c35d5ee2751eab2b3f3f376fbf36.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Community Q&A[/b][/h3][p]Over the past weeks, we’ve received a lot of questions from the community. Here are three of the most interesting ones — with answers:[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: Will there be base building in the game? If so, in what form?[/b][/p][p][b]A:[/b] We explored several concepts early on — from classic "grid-style" construction to block-based settlement building. However, we ultimately decided to steer away from survival-style base building. [i]Neverseas[/i] is a game about sailing, not hopping between outposts and stacking firewood — especially when fast travel and supply returns are involved.[/p][p]That said, construction isn’t entirely off the table. The in-game economy includes the ability to build forts and production sites in friendly cities. These structures will provide various benefits — economic, political, or strategic.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: In a past devlog, you said that no ship is randomly spawned. So... will there be pirate ships at all? How do they fit into a logical world?[/b][/p][p][b]A:[/b] Great question! Our goal is to make [i]Neverseas[/i] a living system — every ship, fleet, or convoy has a reason to exist. But that doesn’t mean randomness is bad — it just has to be meaningful. That’s where our [b]Game Director[/b] system comes in.[/p][p]Inspired by Valve’s [i]Left 4 Dead[/i], our Game Director monitors not just the player, but also the factions. If the world starts drifting into imbalance — for example, if one faction grows too strong — the system responds.[/p][p]Here’s how:[/p][list][*][p][b]Overgrown factions[/b]: If a faction builds up too much power — a giant navy, stockpiles of resources — but fails to maintain logistics (say, due to the player attacking supply lines), some of its ships may [b]mutiny[/b], becoming pirate fleets hostile to everyone.[/p][/*][*][p][b]External threats[/b]: As the world expands, new regions will unlock. From these, [b]independent pirate armadas[/b] may enter the world, not to conquer — but to burn and pillage.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Lost ships[/b]: Although the world of [i]Neverseas[/i] is isolated, it’s not sealed. From time to time, [b]rogue vessels[/b] may drift into the known seas — some joining factions, others becoming pirates or forming new bands.[/p][/*][/list][p]So, pirates in [i]Neverseas[/i] aren’t just “spawned for gameplay” — they are emergent elements of a dynamic world, born from conflict, imbalance, and opportunity.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Q: Can players equip different types of weaponry on their ships?[/b][/p][p][b]A:[/b] That’s a topic we’ll explore in more detail in the next devlog — but we’ll give you a sneak peek.[/p][p]Each ship in [i]Neverseas[/i] features multiple [b]gun sides[/b] and [b]weapon slots[/b], some of which are unique to its class. You can equip specific types of cannons depending on the ship’s design — but you won’t be able to throw ten 42-pounders onto a tiny sloop (or, well… you could try, but we don’t recommend it 🙂).[/p][p]Currently, players choose:[/p][list][*][p]The [b]type[/b] of weapon for each side (e.g., light carronades, standard cannons, or specialty weapons)[/p][/*][*][p]The [b]number[/b] of weapons within that type, based on the ship’s structure and available space[/p][/*][/list][p]This system mirrors historical naval practices, where most ships were armed symmetrically for practical and tactical reasons. We follow that logic both for immersion and gameplay balance — each new weapon upgrade should feel impactful, not just a stat shuffle.[/p][p]More on ship armaments in our next devlog — stay tuned in two weeks! ⚓[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]If you like the project and want to support what we’re building, feel free to help us through one of the platforms below:[/p][p]💬 [url="https://boosty.to/neverseas"]Boosty[/url]
🎁 [url="https://www.patreon.com/c/Neverseas"]Patreon[/url][/p][hr][/hr][p]Thanks for reading all the way to the end!
With respect,
[b]The Neverseas Development Team[/b][/p]

notes.title: Optimization: DLSS and FidelityFX SR
notes.content:
[h2]Optimization and Performance[/h2]
Lately we have received many reports of poor performance in the game on some machines. I hope you didn't wait too long, because all this time we have been working on optimization and performance. As a result, DLSS and FSR were integrated into the project, significantly increasing performance, as well as a number of other optimization edits that allowed us to gain a certain number of frames without losing image quality.
[h3]DLSS[/h3]
The DLSS image enhancement algorithm allows you to increase the maximum resolution values, which ultimately directly affects the “playability” of the content and promotes deep immersion in it.
[h3]Fidelity FX Super Resolution[/h3]
Fidelity FX Super Resolution is a real-time image scaling technology that allows you to increase productivity with minimal loss of final image quality.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Updates and changes[/h2]
New control tips and new content have also been added:
[list]
[*] The ship interface has been redesigned: it now has control tips and only the necessary information is displayed
[*] The character interface has been redesigned, namely, a hint on the main keys for interacting with interfaces and the outside world has been added.
[*] Now there is no need to hold down the compass key. Now it is always displayed. You can also turn off its display using the C key.
[*] Added interface for tasks and orders. Now you can prioritize the tasks you are performing and hide those that you plan to do later or completely refuse to complete them.
[*] A spyglass has been added, allowing you to see threats in time and adjust the course of your ship
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Bug fixes[/h2]
In addition to this, critical problems were eliminated that prevented players from receiving part of the game’s content:
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where the character would hang in the air when equipping a weapon while controlling the ship
[*] Fixed a bug where NPCs disappeared after talking to them
[*] Fixed a bug where it was possible to skip the starting tasks and sail on a ship, thereby breaking the passage
[*] Fixed a bug due to which NPC weapons glowed as an item for pickup
[*] Fixed a bug due to which additional cannons could fire in a circle
[*] Fixed a bug where islands did not appear while sailing on a ship
[/list]

[i][b]Have a nice FPS, Captain![/b][/i]

tags.feature: Lately we have received many reports of poor performance in the game on some machines. I hope you didn't wait too long, because all this time we have been working on optimization and performance. As a result, DLSS and FSR were integrated into the project, significantly increasing performance, as well as a number of other optimization edits that allowed us to gain a certain number of frames without losing image quality.
The DLSS image enhancement algorithm allows you to increase the maximum resolution values, which ultimately directly affects the “playability” of the content and promotes deep immersion in it.
Fidelity FX Super Resolution is a real-time image scaling technology that allows you to increase productivity with minimal loss of final image quality.
The ship interface has been redesigned: it now has control tips and only the necessary information is displayed
The character interface has been redesigned, namely, a hint on the main keys for interacting with interfaces and the outside world has been added.
Now there is no need to hold down the compass key. Now it is always displayed. You can also turn off its display using the C key.
Added interface for tasks and orders. Now you can prioritize the tasks you are performing and hide those that you plan to do later or completely refuse to complete them.
A spyglass has been added, allowing you to see threats in time and adjust the course of your ship

notes.title: Festival update
notes.content:
Recently, a system for creating items has been added, the initial tasks have been updated, which will allow you to immerse yourself in the world of Neverseas easier and more enjoyable, as well as a world-building system and much more. Our main goal with this update is to simplify controls, as well as provide you with more tips on how to control and interact with our game world. Separately, on behalf of the studio, we would like to express our gratitude to all the players who provided feedback through our Discord or video on Youtube.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]We have also made content updates to the current version of the game.[/h2]

[table noborder=1]
    [tr]
        [td style="width: 30"] 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/be0f174c52a7222459856f6dcccd51e4a87655f5.png[/img] 
        [/td]
        [td] Added item creation system. Now you can create materials and equipment that will help you in battles with opponents both at sea and on land.[/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td] 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/7c37a43c33b7d6cf587e4f85dcada17e526abe09.png[/img]
        [/td]
        [td] Добавлен новый корабельный модуль - Корабельная Сеть. В различных ее вариациях она сможет Вам помочь с восполнением ресурсов для команды или со сбором ресурсов для крафта.[/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td] 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/fdfcfc491ef29cd171dd5d20f147e96770d3c150.png[/img]
        [/td]
        [td] Added a new ship module - Ship Network. In its various variations, it can help you with replenishing resources for the team or collecting resources for crafting.[/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td] 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45021039/67161d65e1d82688ec8af3f3156df17d5d32f52f.png[/img]
        [/td]
        [td] Additional tasks have been added in the form of orders that can be given to you by merchants and island residents.[/td]
    [/tr]
[/table] 

[hr][/hr]

[h2]And thanks to your feedback, some changes have been made to existing systems[/h2]
[list]
[*] The interface of the store window has been redesigned.
[*] Interaction options have been improved, so you no longer have to choose between picking up an item or talking to an island resident.
[*] The sight on the ship has been changed. Now at night it is visible more clearly and brightly.
[*] Added many control hints or hints to various systems.
[*] The game settings have been completed. Now all the sliders and checkboxes in the settings work correctly!
[*] The localization work is almost complete.
[*] And many other small changes that we hope will make the game more convenient and enjoyable.
[/list]

[h3][i]Good luck in your new campaigns Captain![/i][/h3]
